findings: File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py, Line: 133, Issue: Config semantics: In the new "thread-queue-parallel" mode, `num_queues=max_workers or 20` reuses the `max_workers` parameter (documented elsewhere as a thread-pool size for "batched-parallel") as the number of queues, and silently falls back to 20 when it is not provided. Callers configuring `max_workers` for one mode and switching modes will get very different parallelism, and the implicit default of 20 queues is not surfaced anywhere. Consider a dedicated parameter or an explicit constant with a comment explaining the default.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py, Line: 118, Issue: Unused allocation: `self.result_processor = self.result_processor_cls()` is now constructed unconditionally at the top of `__init__`, but in "serial", "parallel", and "batched-parallel" modes the instance is never passed to any worker (only `thread-queue-parallel` uses it via `FixedQueuePool`). If `result_processor_cls()` is expensive or holds resources (connections, threads), this adds unnecessary overhead per factory for all other modes. If it is cheap and stateless this is harmless, but worth confirming.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 138, Issue: Data loss on processing errors: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block always calls `complete_offset`, even when `result_processor` raised an exception. The exception is only logged, so the offset becomes committable and the commit loop will advance past a message that was never successfully processed — the message is silently dropped. Combined with `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`'s exception handler (which marks the offset complete on any decode/submit error), any transient failure (e.g., a network blip inside `result_processor`) results in permanent data loss rather than retry or consumer restart. If at-least-once semantics are intended, failed offsets should remain outstanding (or the failure should propagate so the consumer can be restarted).

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 253, Issue: No backpressure: The docstring of `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but `FixedQueuePool` uses unbounded `queue.Queue` instances and `submit` never blocks or checks depth. If workers are slower than the Kafka consumer, queues grow without limit and memory usage is unbounded. Either use bounded queues (with `put` blocking, which also provides real backpressure via arroyo's submit) or remove the guarantee from the docstring and add a max-depth guard.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 130, Issue: Ordering broken on error: When `result_processor` fails for an item, the worker logs and continues to the next item in the same queue. Since the failed offset is marked complete (see the data-loss issue), subsequent messages for the same group are processed and committed even though an earlier message for that group failed — violating the "Items for the same group are processed in order / no item lost" guarantee stated in the class docstring. A realistic trigger: one malformed or temporarily-unprocessable payload for a monitor group causes its later updates to be applied out of order.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 297, Issue: Assert in hot path: `submit` uses `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` to obtain the partition/offset. Asserts are stripped when Python runs with `-O`, in which case `message.value.partition` would raise `AttributeError` (caught by the broad handler, silently dropping the message). Use an explicit `if not isinstance(...)` check with logging instead.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 343, Issue: join semantics: `join()` calls `self.close()`, which performs a full shutdown (sets shutdown event, joins commit thread, shuts down the queue pool). In arroyo's `ProcessingStrategy` contract, `join` is expected to wait for in-flight work after `close`/`terminate`, not to trigger shutdown itself. Calling `join()` on a strategy that was already closed re-runs `queue.shutdown()` and `worker.join()` (mostly harmless due to the try/except, but `close()` being invoked twice via `join` after `close` is redundant), and calling `join()` alone shuts down a strategy the caller may not have intended to stop.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 116, Issue: Flaky assertion: `test_different_groups_distributed` asserts that 20 group keys map to exactly 3 distinct queue indices. Unless the hashing/distribution logic in `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` guarantees perfect spread, a hash function can legitimately map all 20 keys to fewer than 3 queues, making this assertion flaky. If the implementation doesn't guarantee coverage of every queue, the test should assert `len(queue_indices) >= 1` or use keys known to spread.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 197, Issue: Race condition in test: In `test_stats_reporting`, immediately after submitting 10 items the test asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. Worker threads may have already consumed and processed some or all items by the time `get_stats()` runs, making `total_items` 0 and failing the assertion intermittently. The check should be removed or made tolerant (e.g., only assert the final `total_items == 0` after the completion event).

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 1689, Issue: Resource leak on failure: In every new `test_thread_queue_parallel_*` test, `factory.shutdown()` is called after the assertions rather than in a `finally` block. If any assertion fails (e.g., the polling loop times out and `assert mock_processor_call.call_count == 2` raises), `shutdown()` never runs, leaving worker threads and the queue pool alive for the rest of the test session. Wrapping the test body in `try/finally` with `factory.shutdown()` in the `finally` would make failures safe.

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 1714, Issue: Flaky timing-based waits: The polling loops (e.g., `max_wait = 50` with `time.sleep(0.1)`, or `max_wait = 20` in the offset tests) rely on wall-clock timeouts to wait for asynchronous background processing. On slow or loaded CI machines these fixed budgets can expire before workers finish, causing intermittent failures that don't indicate a real bug. Consider waiting on a deterministic signal (e.g., an event set by the mocked processor, or joining the worker threads) instead of sleep-based polling.

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 1830, Issue: Assertion after timeout may pass vacuously: In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, the loop breaks when `mock_processor_call.call_count >= 2` and then sleeps 0.2s before asserting `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. This is a negative assertion checked after a fixed delay — a commit that arrives slightly later than 0.2s would be missed, making the test pass even if the implementation incorrectly commits past a failed message. The same pattern exists in `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` (sleep 0.2 after break before asserting commits stay <= 101).

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 2050, Issue: Private API usage in integration test: The Kafka integration test drives `StreamProcessor` via `processor._run_once()` and `processor._shutdown()`, which are private methods and may change without notice, breaking this test independently of the feature under test. If a public run/stop API exists on `StreamProcessor`, prefer it; otherwise this coupling should be noted.

Consider also breaking when the fetched ID set is empty or when a batch deletes fewer rows than fetched, or bounding iterations.

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go, Line: 547, Issue: MaxCount semantics changed: The old single-statement approach deleted at most `MaxCount` rows per execution pass with a fixed OFFSET, relying on the outer loop. The new per-batch flow re-issues `LIMIT batch OFFSET MaxCount` on every iteration while rows are being deleted; because deleting rows shifts the effective offset window, successive batches can reach progressively older annotations, so the total deleted across the loop may exceed `MaxCount` by more than the old behavior did. If the intent is "keep at most MaxCount annotations", consider recomputing the offset/limit each iteration (e.g., `LIMIT batch OFFSET MaxCount - deletedSoFar` clamped to >= 0) or capping total deletions at `MaxCount`.

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go, Line: 237, Issue: Test fragility: `createTestAnnotations` now assigns explicit IDs (`ID: int64(i + 1)`) while `fakeSQL` is initialized once and shared across all subtests. Rows are deleted between subtests via the `t.Cleanup`, but auto-increment/sequence counters are not reset on all backends (e.g., MySQL InnoDB keeps its counter). Explicit IDs lower than the counter are accepted by most engines, so this likely works, but it relies on backend-specific behavior; if any insert fails on a particular test database (e.g., a backend that rejects duplicate explicit IDs after a failed/partial prior subtest), the failure will be confusing. Using auto-generated IDs (as before) would be more robust.
